    Conditions signalled by harbouR

    Source: R/conditions.R
    harbouR-conditions.Rd

    Every error harbouR raises itself, and every HTTP or transport failure, carries the class harbour_error, plus a more specific subclass, so callers can react to what went wrong rather than matching on message text. Errors from argument matching in rlang - a value that is not one of an argument's choices, or an argument passed in ... that the function does not have - keep the classes rlang gives them.

    Condition classes

    harbour_error_auth

    Credentials are missing, malformed, or were rejected by the server. Fields: status, url and response_body when the server refused them; none when the problem was caught before any request. The token exchanges refuse credentials with whatever status their endpoint uses - a wrong password is HTTP 400, an unknown API token HTTP 403 - and such an error carries harbour_error_http or harbour_error_permission as well.

    harbour_error_http

    The server returned a non-2xx status that has no more specific subclass, or the request got no complete answer (status NA). Fields: status, url and response_body - the parsed JSON, or the text when the server did not send JSON. It is also raised for a redirect (a 3xx status), which harbouR reports rather than follows, and for a reply that is not JSON whatever its status, a 2xx included; response_body then holds the start of its text. A request that got no answer - a refused connection, a DNS or TLS failure, a timeout, a dropped connection - also carries httr2's classes httr2_failure and httr2_error, and has no response_body. After a timeout or a dropped connection the server may already have applied a write, so a status of NA alone does not make sending the write again safe.

    harbour_error_not_found

    HTTP 404, or a named table, view or column that does not exist in the base. Fields: status, url, response_body for the HTTP case.

    harbour_error_permission

    HTTP 403. The token is not allowed to do this. Fields: status, url, response_body.

    harbour_error_rate_limit

    HTTP 429. Fields: status, url, response_body.

    harbour_error_bad_argument

    An argument failed validation before any request was made. Fields: none.

    harbour_error_unsupported

    The operation is not available - for example an auth mode that this endpoint does not accept.

    harbour_error_column_collision

    A column in the data would collide with a reserved SeaTable field name.

    harbour_error_package_asset

    A packaged branding asset is missing from the installation. Field: file.

    All of them also inherit from harbour_error and from rlang_error.

    Warning classes

    The warnings a script may want to check for, or to silence, carry a class of their own, and inherit from rlang_warning:

    harbour_warning_unknown_column

    hb_append_rows() was given columns the table does not have, and drops them.

    harbour_warning_hidden_columns

    hb_read_table() read through a view on a server, which leaves the columns the view hides out of its rows, so they are NA.

    harbour_warning_view_filters

    hb_read_table() read through a filtered view of a .dtable file that records no rows for it, so every row was returned.

    harbour_warning_query_limit

    hb_query() ran SQL without a LIMIT clause, so SeaTable returned at most 100 rows.

    harbour_warning_non_finite

    hb_append_rows() or hb_update_rows() sent Inf, -Inf or NaN, which JSON cannot hold, as null. Field: columns.

    harbour_warning_checkbox_value

    hb_append_rows() or hb_update_rows() sent a checkbox string that as.logical() cannot read as TRUE or FALSE as null. Field: columns.

    harbour_warning_asset_link

    hb_write_dtable() left symbolic links in the asset tree out of the archive.

    harbour_warning_dtable_tz

    hb_read_table() read date-times from a .dtable that carry no time zone, as a server's export stores them, as UTC, because options(harbouR.dtable_tz) names none. Given once a session.

    harbour_warning_json_keys

    hb_write_dtable() met object keys that JSON cannot keep - empty, or repeated - so those values change on the way to disk.

    harbour_warning_json_text

    hb_read_dtable() met a NUL character in content.json, which R cannot keep in a string.

    harbour_warning_id_column

    hb_dtable(), hb_read_csv() or hb_read_xlsx() dropped a column named _id that held values other than SeaTable row ids.

    Examples

    res <- tryCatch(
  hb_client(server = "https://example.org", api_token = NULL),
  harbour_error_auth = function(cnd) "no credentials"
)
res
#> [1] "no credentials"
